findings.body:
`InsecureSkipVerify: true` is hard-coded in `NewClient()` with no environment, build-tag, or config guard. Every consumer of this client — including production — will accept any TLS certificate, enabling MITM on ledger HTTPS traffic.

A comment referencing staging and TICKET-77 does not limit runtime behavior. If staging needs a self-signed cert, trust that CA via `RootCAs` (or gate skip-verify behind an explicit non-prod flag that defaults off and fails closed in prod).

```suggestion
		Transport: &http.Transport{
			TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12},
			Proxy: http.ProxyFromEnvironment,
		},
```

(The suggestion restores verification; wire staging trust via `RootCAs` or a separate staging-only client rather than skip-verify.)

Assigning a bare `&http.Transport{}` replaces the default transport and loses proxy-from-environment, reasonable idle-conn defaults, and HTTP/2 configuration from `http.DefaultTransport`.

When you customize TLS, clone `http.DefaultTransport` (or set `Proxy: http.ProxyFromEnvironment` and the usual limits explicitly) so skip-verify is not the only behavioral change.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge as-is.** `NewClient()` now disables TLS certificate verification for every caller, with no environment, build tag, or configuration gate. A comment and `TICKET-77` do not constrain runtime behavior — any production binary that uses this client will accept any certificate, including an attacker’s.

## Why this is blocking

`internal/ledger/client.go` sets `tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true}` on the client’s transport. That turns off server identity checks for all HTTPS ledger traffic from this client. On a component named “ledger,” intercepted or redirected traffic can be read or altered without TLS detecting it.

The PR description frames this as a staging-only workaround for a self-signed cert. The code path is unconditional: `NewClient()` takes no env/option and always installs skip-verify. Staging convenience shipped this way becomes a permanent foot-gun the moment the same artifact or package is used outside staging.

## Secondary note

Replacing `Transport` with a bare `&http.Transport{}` also drops `http.DefaultTransport` defaults (proxy-from-env, HTTP/2, idle connection limits). Worth fixing when the TLS approach is corrected; not the primary blocker.

## What “fixed” looks like

Prefer one of:
- Trust the staging CA explicitly (`RootCAs` pool) or pin the staging cert.
- Gate skip-verify behind an explicit staging-only config that defaults to secure and cannot be on in prod (fail closed).
- Use a separate staging constructor/test helper that never ships in the production client.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: NewClient() hard-codes tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true} with only a staging comment and no env/build/config guard; the base version used a default http.Client that verified certs, so this is a real unconditional MITM risk.
